subject.title: [Feature]: Skill lifecycle management — auto-optimization on failure + usage-based retirement

question: Should OpenClaw own skill auto-optimization and usage-based retirement in core, expose plugin/ClawHub APIs for it, or defer the direction for now?
rationale: The request adds durable run-derived learning, skill visibility/archive/delete policy, and new config/state surfaces, which repository policy treats as product and compatibility decisions rather than a narrow repair.

options.title: Design boundary first
options.body: Keep this issue open for a maintainer design that splits failure repair from retirement metrics and decides the core/plugin API and storage contracts before implementation.

options.title: Core-owned lifecycle feature
options.body: Sponsor a core Skill Workshop extension with tested migrations, config docs, and conservative default-off archive/delete behavior.

options.title: Defer outside core
options.body: Ask for a plugin or ClawHub prototype first and only revisit core if current extension APIs are insufficient.

recommendation.title: Design boundary first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for a maintainer design that splits failure repair from retirement metrics and decides the core/plugin API and storage contracts before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has recent product-direction work on Skill Workshop suggestions, `/learn`, and prompt/tool policy, making him the best available decision owner from the history sampled.
